title: Vendor-neutral DDIL test and conformance harness for tactical software (link emulation, multi-node TAK/CoT sync scoring, pre-Jailbreak API contract tests, TAK plugin RBAC/audit conformance)
status: KILLED as a venture (G29-score.json verdict: kill, market attractiveness 2.4, founder fit 4.2). This GTM file designs ONLY for the narrower surviving version and is explicitly a credibility-and-validation path, not a company plan.
version_designed_for: The narrower version named in G29-score.json 'narrower_version_if_borderline': an open-source 'TAK DDIL bench' (Linux netem or NRL EMANE/CORE link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps, ~8-10 containerised ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes, scripted partitions and reconnect storms, a sync-scoring report) plus an ATAK plugin RBAC/audit/SBOM conformance module emitting a signed OSCAL-style bundle, sized at $30-60k and 3-4 months, used (a) to sell a handful of fixed-fee pre-sprint readiness runs to Jailbreak-series vendors, (b) as the entry into a C5ISR Center NetModX persistent-experimentation slot or an xTech hackathon, and (c) as the credibility asset that gets the founders into an NGC2 team-member T&E cell, a prime T&E cell or a TAK plugin shop. No government purchase is expected; any lab adoption is a relationship, not revenue. Every milestone below tests the decisive doubt: does ANY named buyer with a budget line or vehicle exist for a neutral harness? The default expectation, per the score file, is that the answer is no and the 90-day plan ends with a documented kill and a reusable open-source asset.

links.value: Tactical software resilience under DDIL (1 Mbps to 1 kbps, partitions, reconnect storms) and conformance to government-baselined TAK/CoT and NGC2 interfaces plus the Army AO's RBAC/audit expectations are still proven live at in-person events, not by a reproducible pre-event test.
links.detail: FACT: Operation Jailbreak (Fort Carson, May 2026) gathered ~600 participants from 50+ firms to expose and document APIs across 70+ Army capabilities (DefenseScoop 2026-05-29; ExecutiveGov). FACT: at Ivy Sting 5 / Lightning Surge 2 (2026-03) industry partners were 'fixing the code in almost real time' (DVIDS 2026-03-30). FACT: an Army CTO/AO memo (2025-09-05, reported 2025-10-03) rated the NGC2 prototype 'very high risk' over unassessed third-party apps lacking access control and audit logging (CNBC; RECALL from G14, not re-verified this session). The pain is real but episodic and is absorbed by exercise hours and engineer time, not by a line item.

links.value: Integration/test engineers at small sensor, vehicle and app vendors preparing for a Jailbreak-series sprint or NGC2 onboarding; NGC2 team-lead T&E engineers (Team Anduril / Team Lockheed Martin); government T&E engineers at DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC and the CJSIL at Aberdeen Proving Ground and the Huntsville software integration lab; TAK plugin developers using the TAK.gov third-party pipeline.
links.detail: FACT: Jailbreak participants (MatrixSpace 2026-06-02, Adyton 2026-09-25, AeroVironment 2026-07-27, Red Hat) describe validation as in-person demonstration through documented interfaces. FACT: the Army plans to harden 74+ jailbroken capabilities at software integration labs in Huntsville, AL and Aberdeen Proving Ground, MD (army.mil/article/294250, 2026). The users exist and are numerous (50-80 firms per event) but each faces the deadline only a few times a year.

links.value: Nobody owns a requirement for a NEUTRAL harness. The underlying DDIL-resilience and interface-conformance requirements are owned by CPE C2IN (NGC2 acquirer), the Army CTO (Right to Integrate / API Marketplace) and the Army authorizing official (RBAC/audit), with ATEC as the evaluator of record.
links.detail: FACT: ATEC established an NGC2 integration environment inside the Combined Joint Systems Integration Laboratory (CJSIL) at APG with DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ran the first Data Layer Assessment of the NGC2 prototypes from October 2025 to February 2026, harvests prototype data in near real time and delivers assessment reports within 1-2 weeks of an event (army.mil/article/295218 'ATEC transforms Test and Evaluation for NGC2', 2026, retrieved 2026-09-26). FACT: C5ISR Center's 'Radio Rodeo' (March-April 2026) used laboratory and field infrastructure to test industry radios for EW resilience in support of NGC2 (army.mil/article/293742, 2026-07). INFERENCE: the requirement owners have chosen to satisfy these requirements with government labs and prime T&E, so the 'requirement' for an outside scorer does not exist; a startup can only offer to make the government's own gate cheaper for vendors.

links.value: BREAK. No RFI, sources sought, BAA topic, CSO, OTA or task order for a vendor-neutral DDIL/conformance harness was found (searches 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-26). The one solicited rail (SBIR via xTech) is ownership-gated for this cap table (13 CFR 121.702) and already assigned. Hypothetical rails: a CRADA/NetModX persistent-experimentation slot (no funds), a subcontract inside an NGC2 team lead's prototype OTA (Anduril $99.6M 2025-07-18; Lockheed Martin $26M 2025-09-02), or a vendor B2B purchase order (no vehicle needed, $5-25k per engagement, INFERENCE).
links.detail: FACT: SBIR/STTR was reauthorised 2026-04-13 through 2031-09-30 and Army FUZE posted five funding opportunities (Crowell; insidegovernmentcontracts.com 2026-04), but eligibility still requires >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership and control (13 CFR 121.702, eCFR) - neither founder's equity counts until the German founder holds permanent residence. FACT: OTA/CSO routes carry no statutory ownership test (10 U.S.C. 3014/4022; DIU CSO) but individual agreements may impose U.S.-person, CUI or ITAR terms. Counsel required; no legal determination made here.

links.value: Government performs the function: ATEC (CJSIL at APG; Data Layer Assessment Oct 2025-Feb 2026; Continuous Evaluation Campaign), DEVCOM C5ISR Center (Radio Rodeo, NetModX persistent experimentation), Huntsville/APG software integration labs, Army Software Factory validation (RECALL). Commercial emulators sold to labs and primes: Keysight EXata/JNE, Apposite, iTrinegy (vendor claims, not verified performance). money_map.weakest_link: contract_vehicle (BREAK) - immediately preceded by a missing program office and budget line. There is no requirement owner for a neutral harness, no office whose mission is to buy test tooling, no PE or sub-line, and no RFI, CSO, OTA or task order; the sole solicited dollar (A254-019, Phase I up to $250k) is SBIR-gated for this cap table and already routed to an established firm. The chain breaks at the exact point where money would change hands.
money_map.penalty_note: Major penalty applies (per G29-score.json). The chain PROBLEM -> USER holds at HIGH confidence, REQUIREMENT OWNER exists only for the underlying requirement (satisfied in-house by ATEC/CJSIL, C5ISR Center and prime T&E), and PROGRAM OFFICE, CONTRACTING OFFICE, BUDGET and VEHICLE are all 'none' or 'Public evidence insufficient' for the harness itself. New evidence this session strengthens the kill: ATEC now runs a long-term system-of-systems NGC2 testbed in the CJSIL with near-real-time data harvesting and 1-2 week assessment reports (army.mil/article/295218, 2026), i.e. the government is investing in exactly the pre-event, continuous evaluation function the harness would sell. Every dollar figure in this map is a request, ceiling or prize, not an obligation to this opportunity.

timeline.event: NGC2 Characteristics of Need / RFI cycle begins (draft SOO, presolicitation feedback, TEM 14); defines a data-centric, app-based C2 stack with government-approved non-proprietary APIs and DDIL operation - the host ecosystem, not a test-tooling ask.

Army SBIR topic A254-019 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' issued (proposals due 2025-03-26; Phase I up to $250,000 for 6 months): a modelling and simulation environment that generates realistic tactical data streams and simulates limited bandwidth producer-to-consumer to model a DDIL environment for NGC2; award eligibility restricted to xTechIgnite winners. The only public solicitation naming DDIL tactical-network test/simulation tooling.
DARPA FLUID program page posted, defining the DDIL regime of interest as 1 Mbps down to 1 kbps for C5ISRT traffic - public specification of the link profiles a harness must reproduce.

xTechIgnite 2025 winners announced (up to 24 x $10,000; eligible to submit SBIR Phase I / D2P2 proposals 2025-06-12 to 2025-07-09); Topic 2 (Generative AI-enabled Tactical Network) winner: Assured Information Security 'GRUNTS'. A prize, not a deployment; Phase I award status not independently confirmed.
Army awards Team Anduril a $99.6M prototype OTA for NGC2 at 4th Infantry Division (11-month period) - the prime-led vehicle inside which team-member T&E is funded (adjacent, not test tooling).
Army awards Team Lockheed Martin a $26M prototype OTA for the NGC2 integrated data layer at 25th Infantry Division (NTE 16 months).

Army CTO/AO memo rates the NGC2 prototype 'very high risk' over unassessed third-party apps lacking access control and audit logging (reported 2025-10-03; RECALL from G14, not re-verified this session) - origin of the RBAC/audit conformance element; the AO, not a vendor, sets and re-tests the bar.

ATEC conducts the first-ever NGC2 Data Layer Assessment inside the CJSIL at Aberdeen Proving Ground, with C5ISR Center; ATEC collection is embedded in each prototype and reports are delivered within 1-2 weeks of events. Government builds the continuous-evaluation capability in-house.

Technical Exchange Meeting 15 (TEM 15), Aberdeen Proving Ground and virtual, hosted by CPE C3N and the C2 Future Capability Directorate; theme 'Aligning to Rapidly Deliver Capability to the Warfighter'; the standing industry-engagement forum for NGC2.
Ivy Sting 4 tests C2 under denied network conditions; Ivy Sting 5 / Lightning Surge 2 (2026-03) with industry 'fixing the code in almost real time' - DDIL failures found live.
C5ISR Center 'Radio Rodeo': laboratory and field-based challenges testing vehicle-mounted industry radios for EW resilience in support of NGC2 (reported 2026-07).

Army FUZE xTech National Security Hackathon: registration 2026-04-14 to 2026-05-02 09:00 PT, event 2026-05-02/03, up to 700 participants; problem areas include resilient edge operations and mission C2. Prize on-ramp, not a procurement.

Operation Jailbreak at Fort Carson (~600 participants, 50+ firms, 70+ capabilities' APIs exposed); Army API Marketplace launched; ACC-APG C2APPSRFI-1 storefront/pipeline RFI posted 2026-05-12 (no award expected).

NATO CWIX 2026 at JFTC Bydgoszcz: 3,500-4,000 specialists, 41-46 nations, ~780 systems; industry participates through national delegations (e.g., Swiss armasuisse with industry partners). Allied interoperability-testing venue, government-run.

Project Convergence Capstone 6 at NTC (division-scale NGC2 validation; outcomes not retrieved). 2026-07-27: AeroVironment states future Jailbreak sprints will extend to joint forces, allies and partners and that open, documented interfaces are being written into future acquisition contracts.

TAK Offsite 2026, Colorado Springs - annual government TAK community gathering (program offices, developers, international participants, industry) where interoperability challenges are surfaced; no conformance requirement published.

Operation Jailbreak Falcon Fury (ASA(ALT), Army CTO, JIATF-401, CENTCOM) puts vendor entities/events on the API Marketplace (Adyton press release 2026-09-25); TITAN moves to production ($127M Palantir / $65M Anduril delivery orders, 2026-09-01) - illustrating what 'production' looks like for NGC2-adjacent programs. No production or follow-on event exists for test tooling.

procurement_signal.stage: Prototyping (host NGC2/TAK ecosystem) - no procurement sequence exists for the harness itself
procurement_signal.rationale: For the host ecosystem the classic sequence is visible and moving: RFI/CoN (2024-05) -> prototype OTAs (2025-07, 2025-09) -> division-scale exercises and government T&E (2025-10 to 2026-07) -> fielding decisions expected after PC-C6 with a 50% obligation cap and GAO criticism (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20, RECALL) still unresolved; that is Prototyping edging toward Transitioning. For the neutral harness the sequence has never started: the only item that resembles 'sources sought' is A254-019 (2025-02), which asked for a GenAI DDIL data-load simulator, routed a $10k prize and a possible $250k Phase I to another firm, and produced no follow-on that is publicly visible. Every subsequent event (CJSIL Data Layer Assessment, Radio Rodeo, ATEC's 1-2 week reports, Huntsville/APG hardening, C2APPSRFI-1's prime-led pipeline) is the government building the function itself. Absence of a competitor in the cross-vendor scoring layer is not evidence of opportunity. Confidence HIGH on the absence of a procurement sequence; MEDIUM on individual dates taken from search summaries.

entry_sequence.vehicle: Open-source release plus B2B fixed-fee 'pre-sprint readiness runs' (no government vehicle; purchase order or credit card)
entry_sequence.office_or_event: Jailbreak-series vendors (MatrixSpace/Adyton/AeroVironment-class and the 50-80 smaller firms per sprint), reached via the Army API Marketplace participant community, TAK.gov third-party pipeline users, and the CivTAK/ATAK developer community; announce at the next xTech hackathon cycle and the TAK Offsite 2027 (expected August 2027, HYPOTHESIS based on the annual pattern; 2026 edition was 2026-08-18/20).
entry_sequence.timing: Months 0-4 (build and publish); first paid runs targeted 4-8 weeks before whichever Jailbreak-series or Ivy Sting date is next announced (dates for the next sprint are not public as of 2026-09-26; AeroVironment 2026-07-27 says future sprints will extend to joint/allied systems).
entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: No ownership, clearance or CMMC requirement for a B2B sale of software built on public code (ATAK-CIV, TAK Server, EMANE/CORE, netem) and synthetic data. INFERENCE (counsel to confirm): the harness is EAR99-type software on public inputs, so the non-U.S.-person founder can build and sell it; any vendor who wants to feed real PoR radio traces, SRW/WNW EMANE waveform models or CUI ICDs into the bench must do so under their own handling rules and the startup must keep the Indonesian founder walled off by a technology control plan. Do not accept CUI into the company before a NIST SP 800-171 self-assessment (DFARS 252.204-7012/7019; CMMC Level 2 self-assessment phase runs to 2026-11-09, Phase 2 C3PAO suspended 2026-07-13).
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: Users, comparable anonymised results and the first test of willingness to pay ($5-25k per engagement, INFERENCE). It does NOT yield a government buyer; it yields the evidence needed to approach one (step 2) and the kill/continue signal for the venture question.

entry_sequence.vehicle: CRADA-based participation in DEVCOM C5ISR Center NetModX persistent experimentation (no funds flow) OR unpaid/low-fee adoption inside an NGC2 team-member T&E cell (subcontract-scale, six figures at most, INFERENCE)
entry_sequence.office_or_event: DEVCOM C5ISR Center, Aberdeen Proving Ground: NetModX persistent-experimentation campaign (the 2025 campaign 'continues into 2026'; the 2027 call has not been published as of 2026-09-26 - HYPOTHESIS that a call appears in Q1 2027 as in prior years); ATEC/CJSIL NGC2 integration environment (approached through a team lead, not directly); Team Anduril and Team Lockheed Martin NGC2 T&E/data-layer leads (Team Anduril members include Palantir, Microsoft, Govini, Striveworks, Instant Connect Enterprise, Research Innovations Inc., Rune Technologies). Named events to attend: TEM 16 (expected late 2026 or early 2027 at APG, HYPOTHESIS from the TEM 15 date of 2026-01-29/30), AFCEA TechNet Augusta (annual, August), the next xTech hackathon (2026 edition was 2026-05-02/03).
entry_sequence.timing: Months 3-9: apply to NetModX persistent experimentation as soon as the 2027 call opens; pitch NGC2 team-member T&E leads with step-1 results 6-8 weeks before Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge iterations.
entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: CRADAs have no statutory ownership test but the lab decides what data it shares; any controlled waveform models or exercise captures require U.S.-person handling, so the German founder (post-permanent-residence) or a U.S.-person hire must be the point of contact for controlled inputs. Subcontracts under a prime's prototype OTA carry flow-down clauses (DFARS 252.204-7012 by reference is common) and possibly CUI - plan for a NIST SP 800-171 self-assessment and SPRS score. FOCI review is only triggered if a facility clearance is later sought. Counsel required; constraint description, not a legal judgment.
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: The only credible route to a government or prime T&E engineer treating the bench's report as pre-event evidence. It produces a named-lab relationship, possibly access to realistic link profiles under the lab's control, and the decisive test of the doubt: if C5ISR Center, ATEC/CJSIL or a team lead will not even run the bench for free, no buyer exists.

entry_sequence.vehicle: Army xTech prize -> SBIR Phase I / Direct-to-Phase-II ONLY IF the cap table is restructured to satisfy 13 CFR 121.702; otherwise an OTA-based subcontract or a DIU CSO response as a team member (no statutory ownership test)
entry_sequence.office_or_event: Army FUZE SBIR|STTR / xTech program office (xTechIgnite-style topic competitions; five FUZE funding opportunities posted after the 2026-04-13 reauthorisation); Army Applications Laboratory; DIU CSO (HQ0845-20-S-C001 successor) only if a C2 test-and-evaluation area of interest appears (none found this session); C5 or IWRP-type OTA consortia (membership fees ~$500-2,500/yr, INFERENCE) as a hedge.
entry_sequence.timing: Months 9-18, and only after steps 1-2 produce (a) at least one lab or prime using the bench and (b) a legal opinion that the company is SBIR-eligible at award. If the German founder's permanent residence has not vested, skip SBIR entirely and pursue the subcontract route.
entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: FACT: SBIR/STTR requires a small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (13 CFR 121.702); options and convertibles count as exercised under 13 CFR 121.103; eligibility is self-certified at award with fraud exposure for misstatement (GAO-24-105470). The Indonesian founder's equity never counts and DoD components restrict foreign-national technical participation (AFWERX Open Topic FAQs 2025-07-02) - they cannot be PI on SBIR work. Whether the 2026 reauthorisation (S. 3971) changed the ownership or foreign-ties tests is unverified (HYPOTHESIS/LOW). OTA/CSO: nontraditional-defense-contractor status is automatic for a new company (10 U.S.C. 3014) and there is no ownership test, but agreements officers can impose U.S.-person or CUI terms. Counsel required.
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: If SBIR-eligible: a $150-250k Phase I-scale award (INFERENCE from Army norms; 2026 caps not retrieved) that is the first government dollar for the bench - still not a deployment. If not eligible: a subcontract that pays for adapting the bench to one prime's stack, which is a services engagement, not a product company. Either outcome is compatible only with the 'credibility asset' framing.

entry_sequence.office_or_event: TAK Offsite 2027 (international participants attend; 2026 edition 2026-08-18/20); NATO CWIX 2027 (expected June 2027 at JFTC Bydgoszcz; 2026 edition 2026-06-08/26; entry only through a national delegation or a system owner); Bundeswehr Cyber Innovation Hub (CIHBw) pilot channel and D-LBO integrators (Rheinmetall, blackned) via the German founder; NATO DIANA 2027 challenge call (2026 cohort had a 'Data Assisted Decision Making' challenge; a DDIL/test challenge is not evidenced - HYPOTHESIS).

entry_sequence.eligibility_notes: TAK.gov third-party pipeline is open to anyone not on the Denied Parties List. CWIX and DIANA do not screen founder nationality but national security authorities do; a German GmbH would be needed for EDF/EDIP eligibility and would complicate a later U.S. FOCI picture. Dual structures are heavy for a $250k team (E06 founder analysis). Counsel required.
entry_sequence.what_it_yields: Widens the lab-tool niche to allied TAK users without changing its ceiling; produces a second reference lab at most.

targets.where_to_find: CIHBw open calls; AFCEA Bonn TechNet Europe; ESUT/Behörden Spiegel event lists; NATO JFTC CWIX planning conferences (through a national delegation); LinkedIn German defence-tech clusters (Munich/Bavaria).

targets.role: Former C5ISR Center / ATEC / JITC tactical-network T&E engineer (now advisor or consultant)
targets.why: The score file rates tactical-network T&E credibility as fatal if absent; this person validates link profiles and scoring rubric and opens lab doors.
targets.where_to_find: ITEA membership; LinkedIn 'former C5ISR' / 'former JITC'; NDIA T&E division; university adjunct faculty in systems engineering; veteran networks.

questions: Walk me through the last time you prepared a plugin, feed or app for an Army integration event (Jailbreak, Ivy Sting, NetModX, Radio Rodeo): what did you test the week before, on what network, with which tools, and who ran it?

Tell me about the last failure that was discovered live at the event rather than beforehand - what was it (arrival order, duplicates after reconnect, saturation, a firewall or auth surprise, missing audit events), how long did it take to fix, and what did that cost you in fielding time?
How do you today reproduce a degraded link - 4 kbps, 30-minute partition, reconnect storm - in your own lab? Who set that up, and what happened when you tried to make it repeatable across releases?
When the team lead or the government lab tests your component, what do they send back, in what form, and how long after the event? What do you do with that report?
Show me how a new app gets onto the NGC2 data layer or into the API Marketplace from your side: which documents, sandboxes, sign-offs and people are involved, and where does the most waiting happen?

Describe the last time the AO or an ISSM asked for evidence about access control, audit logging or the software bill of materials for a third-party app - who produced it, in what format, and what did they reject?
What did you use Lattice Sandboxes (or the TAK Server test framework, or EMANE/CORE) for in the last month, and what did you have to build around them yourself?
If ATEC's assessment report arrived showing a defect in your component two weeks after the event, walk me through what happens next in your organisation and on the contract.
Who inside your company or team decides that a component is 'ready' for an event, and what evidence do they look at to decide?

Have you ever paid an outside party for test or emulation capability (Keysight, Apposite, iTrinegy, a lab, a consultant)? Tell me about that purchase - who approved it, what budget it came from, and what it replaced.
How many integration or exercise deadlines does your team face in a year, and which of them would a two-week-earlier warning have changed?

In the government lab (C5ISR Center / CJSIL / Huntsville): walk me through how a vendor's component gets scheduled, instrumented and scored today, and what tooling you would refuse to let a vendor bring in.
What data, link profiles or traces would a pre-event test need to be believable to you, and which of those can never leave your lab?
Tell me about the last tool you adopted from outside the lab or the prime - how did it get in, who paid, and what would have stopped it?

first_deployment_path.path: The realistic first 'deployment' is not a government purchase but an ADOPTION: (1) publish the open-source TAK DDIL bench and plugin conformance module; (2) run 3-5 paid or free pre-sprint readiness runs for Jailbreak-series vendors and publish anonymised comparative results; (3) use those results and a former-C5ISR/ATEC advisor to secure a DEVCOM C5ISR Center NetModX persistent-experimentation slot (CRADA, 2027 campaign) or an NGC2 team-member T&E cell agreeing to run the bench before an Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge iteration; (4) bring the bench to the next xTech hackathon and TAK Offsite 2027 as the demonstration artefact. Project Convergence, ANTX, Bold Quest and CWIX are government-run interoperability venues where the bench could only appear inside a participating system owner's delegation, not as its own entry - treat them as later, opportunistic.
first_deployment_path.evidence_it_produces: Evidence for a follow-on decision (not a Series A - the score file rules that out): (a) a reproducible score that predicted, before an event, at least one class of failure later observed live (arrival order, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation on reconnect, missing audit events), with vendor attestation; (b) a written statement from a C5ISR Center, ATEC/CJSIL or team-lead T&E engineer that the report was used as pre-event evidence; (c) paid engagements with logos and prices; (d) an NGC2 team-member or prime subcontract or a NetModX CRADA. For a STRATFI/TACFI-style or DIU production step this would still be insufficient - those require a Phase II or CSO prototype award and a program-office transition memo, neither of which has a path here. What the evidence CAN justify is (i) a small services business, (ii) an acqui-hire or hire into a prime/lab T&E cell, or (iii) redeploying the founders and their credibility to a different gap.
alternatives: NGC2 team-lead demo: a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed Martin T&E engineer runs the bench against a team member's component before an Ivy Sting / Lightning Surge iteration (fastest, requires a warm introduction; yields a prime reference, not revenue).

University or ROTC-adjacent unit pilot: a National Guard signal unit or university ROTC exercise runs ATAK-CIV through the bench's scenarios on commercial hardware (cheap, produces soldier feedback, no acquisition standing).
TAK Offsite 2027 demonstration and CivTAK community adoption of the plugin conformance module (produces community usage numbers and TAK Product Center attention; TPC can replicate it).
Allied buyer: a Bundeswehr D-LBO integrator (Rheinmetall/blackned) or a CWIX 2027 national delegation uses the bench in its own lab (produces an allied reference; needs a German entity or partner).
Anduril Lattice / Ditto partner-adapter route: add adapters and seek listing in their developer ecosystems (produces distribution but hands the incumbent the design).

allied_extension.bigger_with_allies: Marginally, not decisively. TAK is used across NATO and the TAK.gov third-party pipeline is open to non-U.S. persons, so a TAK DDIL bench is exportable as a lab tool to allied TAK users; NATO's CWIX (June 2026: ~780 systems, 46 nations) shows allied interoperability testing is large but government-run; Germany's 2026 defence budget (EUR 82.69bn) and D-LBO (EUR 11.5bn, prime-led through 2029) create integrator T&E demand; the UK's Digital Targeting Web and Asgard framework favour incremental software delivery. But allied T&E is likewise a government or prime function with its own labs and commercial emulators, budgets are smaller and slower (EDF/EDIP 12-18 months to grant), and the Lattice/NGC2/AO-conformance half of the product is U.S.-specific. Allies widen the lab-tool niche without changing its ceiling (E06 verdict: HYPOTHESIS, MEDIUM).
allied_extension.what_changes: Product: drop the NGC2/Lattice/AO modules and keep the TAK/CoT sync scoring and generic DDIL profiles; add FMN/STANAG-oriented message sets only if a CWIX delegation asks. Structure: a German GmbH (or partner) is needed for CIHBw pilots and EDF/EDIP eligibility, which complicates a later U.S. FOCI picture and is heavy for a $250k team; the German founder's U.S. permanent residence may pull management outside the EU for EU control tests (E06, specialist review required). Regulatory: no ITAR on the open core, but the Indonesian founder faces slower German personnel-security processes for any classified role. Go-to-market: through primes, NCIA and national hubs, never standalone.
markets: Germany (CIHBw pilots; D-LBO integrators Rheinmetall/blackned; German founder adjacency) - first allied option, still a lab-tool sale
NATO (CWIX 2027 via a national delegation; DIANA 2027 call if a resilient-C2 or test challenge appears - HYPOTHESIS)
United Kingdom (DASA, Asgard framework, DTW integrators) - open for entry, medium for revenue
Australia (ASCA, AUKUS Pillar II challenges) - only for a U.S./UK/AU-domiciled entity
Japan and Singapore - year-5+ markets, LOW near-term accessibility (E06)

goals: Answer the decisive doubt with evidence, not opinion: does any named office, lab, prime or vendor have money or a vehicle for a neutral DDIL/conformance bench?
Recruit the fatal-if-absent advisor: a former C5ISR Center / ATEC / JITC tactical-network T&E engineer on an equity or small-stipend basis.
Get counsel's written constraint memo on SBIR eligibility (13 CFR 121.702/121.103), the Indonesian founder's role, EAR classification of the open core, and a minimal technology control plan.
deliverables: 12-18 completed workflow interviews across at least 8 of the 12 target roles, transcribed and coded against the 14 questions
Written 'money map v1' naming, for each interviewee, the budget or vehicle they used for their last outside test purchase (or 'none')
Counsel memo received; cap-table scenario model showing whether SBIR eligibility is reachable within 12 months
Event calendar with confirmed dates for TEM 16, NetModX 2027 call, next xTech hackathon, TAK Offsite 2027 and the next Jailbreak-series sprint (or documented that dates are not public)
weeks_1_3.owner: Business founder leads interviews, advisor recruiting and counsel; engineer founder attends every lab/prime interview and drafts the bench architecture in parallel
kill_criteria: KILL if fewer than 2 of the interviewed vendor or prime engineers can name a budget, PO or contract line under which they bought ANY outside test/emulation capability in the last 24 months.

KILL if zero of the government-side interviewees (C5ISR Center, ATEC/CJSIL, Army SWF/CTO pipeline, TAK Product Center) say a vendor-produced pre-event score would be read, and at least one says the CJSIL/NetModX infrastructure already covers it.
KILL if no qualified T&E advisor accepts by day 21 (score file: fatal if absent).
KILL (the venture framing, not the open-source build) if counsel confirms SBIR is unreachable within 12 months AND no non-SBIR sponsor candidate emerged from interviews.

goals: Prove technically that a reproducible score exposes DDIL failures that today surface live, using only public inputs.
Establish which link profiles and scenarios the advisor and at least one lab/prime interviewee consider realistic enough to matter.
deliverables: Dockerised bench v0.1: 8-10 ATAK-CIV emulator / TAK Server nodes behind Linux netem profiles (1 Mbps, 64 kbps, 16 kbps, 4 kbps, 1 kbps) with a YAML scenario language for partition schedules and reconnect storms; EMANE/CORE integration as a stretch goal only
Scorer v0.1 reporting time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicates/conflicts after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect, and a reconcile log, as JSON plus HTML

Experiment log: three public ATAK plugins or open CoT feeds run through a 30-minute 4 kbps partition-and-reconnect scenario, with at least one failure class reproduced across repeated runs (variance reported)
Advisor-reviewed link-profile and rubric note stating what is and is not realistic without controlled data
weeks_4_6.owner: Engineer founder builds and runs; business founder continues 4-6 further interviews (especially prime T&E and TAK Product Center) and starts the vendor pipeline for weeks 10-12
kill_criteria: KILL if the bench cannot reproduce at least one failure class (arrival order, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation) deterministically (same verdict in 4 of 5 repeated runs) by end of week 6.
KILL if the advisor and at least one lab/prime engineer judge that without controlled waveform models or radio traces the scores would not change any decision they make.
KILL if total build cost run-rate projects above $60,000 for the full 90 days (the surviving version is capped at $30-60k).

goals: Turn the experiment into a demonstrable prototype with the conformance module and a contract-test pack, packaged for a vendor to self-run.
Secure written commitments for at least three readiness runs and one lab or prime evaluation.
deliverables: ATAK plugin conformance module v0.1: exercises a plugin with synthetic roles and tagged data, emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and an SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX) as a signed OSCAL-style assessment-results bundle; validated against one open-source ATAK plugin
Contract-test CLI v0.1 for CoT/TAK Server Mission API usage from a capture or spec; public Lattice schema validation included only if an interviewee asked for it
Public repository with documentation, a one-command demo and anonymised week-6 results; permissive licence chosen with counsel (data rights posture for a future SBIR/OTA documented)

Signed statements of intent: 3 vendors for a fixed-fee readiness run (target $5-15k each; free allowed for the first if it yields a named reference) and 1 lab or prime T&E cell agreeing to run the bench before its next event
NetModX 2027 / xTech hackathon / TAK Offsite 2027 applications drafted, with submission as soon as calls open
weeks_7_9.owner: Engineer founder (module, CLI, packaging); business founder (vendor commitments, lab/prime agreement, applications); advisor reviews the OSCAL bundle with an ISSM interviewee
kill_criteria: KILL if fewer than 3 vendors sign a statement of intent by end of week 9, or if all three insist on $0 - that confirms the 'episodic, low-price' market the score file predicted.
KILL if no government lab, ATEC/CJSIL contact or NGC2 team-lead T&E cell agrees in writing to run the bench (free) before an event - this is the direct test of 'no buyer needs it'.
KILL if an ISSM/AO-staff interviewee states the OSCAL-style bundle would carry no standing without government designation and no designation route can be named.

goals: Run the readiness engagements and the lab/prime evaluation; measure whether the report changed a decision.
Produce the final go/no-go memo on the venture question and the disposition of the open-source asset.
deliverables: 3 completed readiness runs with scored reports delivered to vendors, each followed by a 30-minute debrief recording what they changed (or not) as a result
1 lab or prime evaluation completed, with a written statement of whether the report was used and what it would take to be accepted as pre-event evidence
Live demonstration (TEM 16 networking, xTech hackathon, TAK Offsite 2027 or a team-lead session, whichever falls first) with a recorded run and Q&A notes

Final memo: revenue collected, cost to date, named sponsor candidates with budget/vehicle (or 'none'), and a decision among (a) continue as a small services line, (b) donate the bench to the community and pivot the founders to another gap, (c) pursue a subcontract/acqui-hire
If and only if the SBIR path is confirmed reachable: a draft xTech/SBIR white paper aligned to the next Army FUZE topic cycle
weeks_10_12.owner: Business founder runs engagements, debriefs and the memo; engineer founder runs the bench, fixes defects found in engagements and prepares the demo
kill_criteria: KILL if paid revenue by day 90 is under $10,000 total or fewer than 2 vendors say in the debrief that they changed code or configuration because of the report.
KILL if the lab or prime evaluation concludes with no written path to the report being accepted as evidence (no named office, no named event where it would be used).

KILL the venture question definitively if by day 90 no interviewee, lab, prime or office has named a budget line, task order, CSO area, OTA or SBIR topic under which a neutral bench could be bought within 12 months - and record this as the expected outcome, not a surprise.

CONTINUE (as a credibility/services asset only) if 2+ paying vendors, 1 lab/prime user and 1 documented pre-event prediction exist; escalate to a venture conversation ONLY on the milestone in most_important_question.milestone_for_next_2_5m.

most_important_question.build_first: A Dockerised, open-source TAK DDIL bench: 8-10 containerised ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes behind Linux netem (EMANE/CORE optional) profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms, a scorer that reports time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicate or conflicting objects after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect and a reconcile-log audit, plus an ATAK plugin conformance module that emits an RBAC matrix, audit-event coverage and an SBOM as a signed OSCAL-style bundle. Build nothing for Lattice or Ditto until an interviewee asks; keep the whole thing on public code and synthetic data so the non-U.S.-person founder can build it (INFERENCE; counsel to confirm). Cap: $30-60k and 3-4 months.
most_important_question.show_it_to: In this order: (1) three or four small vendors facing the next Jailbreak-series or Ivy Sting date (MatrixSpace/Adyton/AeroVironment-class and smaller API Marketplace participants); (2) one NGC2 team-member T&E engineer (Team Anduril or Team Lockheed Martin) and, through them, the team lead's T&E manager; (3) a DEVCOM C5ISR Center tactical-network S&T lead via the NetModX 2027 persistent-experimentation call and an ATEC/CJSIL integration engineer via the advisor; (4) a TAK Product Center engineer at TAK Offsite 2027. Do not lead with the Army CTO or CPE C2IN leadership - they have no test-tooling requirement to hand you.
most_important_question.demo_proves: That a reproducible, vendor-neutral score exposes, before an event, the specific failure classes that today are discovered live at Jailbreak and Ivy Sting - arrival order of priority objects, duplicate tracks after reconnect, saturation on reconnect, missing audit events - and that the same scenario file yields the same verdict across vendors and repeated runs. It also proves what it cannot do: it cannot reproduce PoR waveform behaviour or exercise captures without a lab sponsor, so realism plateaus at 'generic DDIL'.
most_important_question.why_customer_cares: A small vendor cares because failing at the sprint costs a fielding window and engineer weeks on site (~600 people at Fort Carson for one event), and a two-week-earlier warning is cheap relative to that. A team-lead T&E cell cares because comparable numbers help it triage dozens of members before an iteration. A government lab would care only if the bench saved instrumented lab time - but ATEC now embeds collection in each prototype and reports in 1-2 weeks, and C5ISR Center runs its own DDIL infrastructure, so the government's marginal need is close to zero (FACT: army.mil/article/295218; army.mil/article/293742).
most_important_question.why_incumbent_cant_crush: Honest answer: they can, and the more important point is that they need not bother. Anduril already gives away Lattice Sandboxes; TAK Product Center ships takcl and controls what 'conformant' means; Ditto can publish its own benchmark; C5ISR Center and ATEC/CJSIL own the labs and the acceptance authority. The startup's only differentiator is impartiality across TAK, Lattice and Ditto, which has value only if a government body designates the report as accepted evidence - and no public signal shows one intends to. The asset that is genuinely hard to copy is not the code but the founders' earned relationships with lab and prime T&E engineers and the published, comparable result set; that is a credibility asset and a hiring/acqui-hire lever, not a moat (score file: moat 1, incumbent vulnerability 1).
most_important_question.milestone_for_next_2_5m: Only an external designation would justify $2-5M: a written statement from DEVCOM C5ISR Center, ATEC, the Army CTO/AO or TAK Product Center that the bench's report is accepted pre-event or acceptance evidence, backed by a funded instrument (a task order under ACC-APG, a Phase II-scale SBIR or D2P2 after the cap table is eligible, or a CSO/OTA prototype agreement) AND at least one NGC2 team-lead subcontract to run it across its members - i.e., a named requirement owner, office, budget line and vehicle where today there are none. Measurable form: one signed government instrument of at least $500k plus one prime subcontract, and 10+ paying vendors at $10k+ each within 12 months. No public evidence suggests this event is coming inside the founders' runway; the plan above is designed to detect its absence cheaply and end with a reusable open-source asset and relationships rather than a company.
